name: adv_advtrain_clean
title: PGD adversarial training and robust evaluation, correct - two rules' nearest traps
note: Adversarial training breaks the two assumptions the MLV2xx and MLV3xx families rest on, and both false-positive guards are documented in ISSUE_RULES: MLV202's note (a) for a backward whose gradient goes to a leaf input rather than to parameters, and MLV302's for evaluation that genuinely needs gradients. This file exercises both at once - `pgd_attack` differentiates with respect to `delta` and steps no optimizer, and `evaluate_robust` runs `model.eval()` with autograd ON because the attack it measures IS a gradient computation. It carries no `expected` row and must carry no finding. MLView measures 47 nodes / 59 edges and reports zero findings in `local`; under `--dataflow ip` it adds one honest `truncated` diagnostic saying it did not merge the two call sites of pgd_attack.

forbidden.why: train_epoch calls optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True) at line 86, before the forward

the only parameter update is line 89, immediately after the backward at 88; the gradient inside pgd_attack is taken with torch.autograd.grad against `delta` (line 70), a leaf input, and steps no optimizer by design - MLV202's false-positive note (a)
the order in the batch loop is zero_grad (86) -> backward (88) -> step (89)
the no_grad block at line 71 wraps only the in-place projection of delta; torch.autograd.grad at line 70 is outside it, and loss.backward() at line 88 is in another function
train_epoch accumulates loss.item() at line 90; every other accumulator counts Python ints
evaluate_clean calls model.eval() at line 97 and evaluate_robust calls it at line 116; train_epoch restores model.train() at line 79

evaluate_clean carries the @torch.no_grad() decorator at line 95; evaluate_robust deliberately does not, because the PGD attack it runs is itself a gradient computation - that is MLV302's documented de-rate, and the forward it actually measures is wrapped at line 123
SmallResNet.forward returns the raw Linear output; nothing softmaxes before CrossEntropyLoss
there is no binary cross-entropy in this project
the training loader is built with shuffle=True at line 135
the test loader is built with shuffle=False at line 137
no loader passes num_workers, and the module has an `if __name__ == "__main__"` guard at line 152
every batch is moved with .to(DEVICE) inside all three loops, before any forward
DEVICE is chosen by torch.cuda.is_available() at line 33
seed_everything() at line 36 seeds random, numpy and torch, and the training loader takes an explicit generator seeded at line 132
there is no split call; the train and test sets are built separately, and the loader that shuffles takes generator=
SmallResNet.__init__ calls super().__init__() on its first line
the conv stack is an nn.Sequential, not a plain list
